date: # Fed balance-sheet programmes (and the Treasury's own buybacks): start
name: what was bought.
QE1
what: $1.75tn of agency debt, MBS and (from March 2009) Treasuries.
note: end: the FOMC statement of 16 Mar 2010 (monetary20100316a) says the $1.25tn MBS and about $175bn agency-debt purchases finish by the end of March 2010

name: Operation Twist
what: Sold short Treasuries to buy long ones: lengthened the Fed's holdings without growing them.

name: QE3
what: Open-ended: $40bn a month of MBS, plus $45bn of Treasuries from 2013; tapered through 2014.

name: QT1
what: Let maturing bonds roll off, up to $50bn a month.

name: Reserve management bills
what: $60bn a month of Treasury bills after the repo spike: technically not QE.

name: Covid QE
what: Unlimited at first; about $4.6tn of Treasuries and MBS in two years.
note: size: net purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS "totaled roughly $4.6 trillion" (NY Fed, Lorie Logan speech, 2 Mar 2022, newyorkfed.org/newsevents/speeches/2022/log220302); net purchases ended in early March 2022

name: QT2
what: Runoff up to $95bn a month, slowed in 2024 and 2025, ended 1 December 2025.
note: end: the FOMC statement of 29 Oct 2025 (monetary20251029a) concludes the reduction of holdings on 1 December 2025

name: Reserve management purchases
what: Treasury bill purchases to keep reserves ample after QT ended, about $40bn in the first month.
note: NY Fed statement of 10 Dec 2025 (implementing that day's FOMC directive): purchases start 12 Dec 2025, about $40bn of bills in the first monthly schedule

name: Treasury buybacks
what: The Treasury (not the Fed) buys back older, less-traded bonds for liquidity support and cash management, funded by new issues.
note: Treasury refunding statement of 1 May 2024: first (liquidity support) operation on Wednesday 29 May 2024; cash management buybacks to follow later in 2024
